subject: General Knowledge
topic: Major Rivers, Dams & Hydro Projects in India

questions.stem: The KRISHNA RAJA SAGARA (KRS) Dam, which feeds the famous Brindavan Gardens, is built across which river in Karnataka?

options.option_text: Tungabhadra River in Bellary district of northern Karnataka
Cauvery River at Kannambadi village near Mysuru city
Krishna River flowing through the Raichur district area
Sharavathi River, the source of Jog Falls in Shivamogga

questions.explanation: KRS Dam is built across the Cauvery River at Kannambadi, about 19 km from Mysuru; it was constructed by Mokshagundam Visvesvaraya between 1911–1932. Tungabhadra (Option A) is a common wrong pick because it also flows through Karnataka, but it feeds the Tungabhadra Dam in Hospet, not KRS.

questions.stem: India's tallest dam, the TEHRI DAM (height 260.5 m), impounds which river in the Garhwal Himalayas of Uttarakhand?

options.option_text: Alaknanda River, originating from the Satopanth Glacier
Bhagirathi River, a principal headstream of the Ganga
Mandakini River flowing through Rudraprayag district
Pindar River, which joins the Alaknanda at Karnaprayag

questions.explanation: Tehri Dam is built on the Bhagirathi River (and its tributary Bhilangana) in Tehri Garhwal district. The Bhagirathi is a key headstream of the Ganga and is joined by the Alaknanda at Devprayag. Alaknanda (Option A) is the most tempting wrong answer because it is the other major Ganga headstream, but it is not the river that Tehri Dam impounds.

questions.stem: The FARAKKA BARRAGE on the Ganga in West Bengal was constructed primarily to serve which purpose?

options.option_text: Generate hydroelectric power for eastern India's power grid
Divert Ganga water to flush silt from the Hooghly channel
Provide irrigation water to drought-prone districts of Bihar
Create a freshwater reservoir for Kolkata's drinking supply

questions.explanation: Farakka Barrage, commissioned in 1975, was designed to divert Ganga water into the Hooghly (Bhagirathi) river to flush the accumulated silt and maintain the navigability of Kolkata Port. It has no power-generation component (Option A). The barrage became a long-standing dispute with Bangladesh over dry-season flow reduction, leading to the 1996 Ganga Water Treaty.

questions.stem: The POLAVARAM MULTI-PURPOSE PROJECT — declared a national project in 2014 — is being constructed on which river in Andhra Pradesh?

options.option_text: Krishna River at the Andhra Pradesh–Telangana border zone
Godavari River in the West Godavari–Eluru district area
Tungabhadra River near Kurnool in the Rayalaseema region
Mahanadi River in the lower basin near the Odisha coast

questions.explanation: Polavaram Project is built on the Godavari River in the Eluru and West Godavari districts of Andhra Pradesh; it will also serve as a diversion project linking Godavari and Krishna. The Krishna River (Option A) already has the Nagarjuna Sagar and Srisailam dams — it is a frequent wrong choice because both rivers run through AP.

questions.stem: Which Indian dam is most closely associated with RESERVOIR-INDUCED SEISMICITY (RIS), after a destructive M 6.3 earthquake struck near its reservoir in December 1967?

options.option_text: Tehri Dam on Bhagirathi in the seismically active Garhwal zone
Koyna Dam on Koyna River in Maharashtra's Satara district
Nagarjuna Sagar Dam on the Krishna River in Telangana state
Rihand Dam on Son River in Sonbhadra district of Uttar Pradesh

questions.explanation: The 1967 Koyna earthquake (M 6.3) killed ~180 people and is the most studied case of reservoir-induced seismicity (RIS) globally; the NGRI has maintained a seismic monitoring network there since. Tehri Dam (Option A) is located in a naturally seismic Himalayan zone — seismicity there is tectonic, not reservoir-induced — making it the classic distractor.

questions.stem: The RANJIT SAGAR DAM (Thein Dam) — Punjab's tallest dam — is built on which river near the Punjab–Himachal Pradesh border?

options.option_text: Sutlej River, which feeds the Bhakra–Nangal dam system
Ravi River, a westward-flowing tributary of the Indus basin
Beas River, which merges with the Sutlej at Harike wetlands
Chenab River, the longest of the five Punjab river tributaries

questions.explanation: Ranjit Sagar Dam (completed 2001) is built on the Ravi River near the village of Thein in Pathankot district, Punjab, at its border with Himachal Pradesh. Under the Indus Waters Treaty, the Ravi is one of India's three 'eastern rivers'. Sutlej (Option A) is the most common error because Bhakra–Nangal is Punjab's most famous dam system, but that is on the Sutlej, not the Ravi.

questions.stem: The IDUKKI ARCH DAM — one of Asia's largest double-curvature arch dams — is built on which river forming a deep-gorge reservoir in Kerala?

options.option_text: Bharathapuzha River flowing through Palakkad into Tamil Nadu
Periyar River flowing through the Idukki gorge in Kerala
Pamba River originating from Peerumade in the high ranges
Chaliyar River draining into Beypore estuary near Kozhikode

questions.explanation: Idukki Dam (168.91 m, commissioned 1976) is a double-curvature arch dam built on the Periyar River in the narrow gorge between Kuravan and Kurathi hills in Idukki district; it is the first arch dam built in Asia and powers the Moolamattom powerhouse. Pamba (Option C) is the most tempting wrong answer because it also originates in the same Idukki high-range area, but it is not the river that the arch dam impounds.

questions.stem: The HIRAKUD DAM — completed in 1956 on the Mahanadi River in Odisha — is best known for which record or distinctive engineering characteristic?

options.option_text: It is the tallest dam in India at 260.5 metres — taller than the Tehri Dam
It was built exclusively for hydropower with a capacity of 2,000 MW
It stretches about 26 km making it one of the longest dams in the world
It is India's only double-curvature arch dam — a unique engineering feature

questions.explanation: C is correct. Hirakud Dam (completed 1956) measures approximately 25.8 km including earthen dykes and saddle dams, making it the longest dam in India and one of the longest in the world. Option A is wrong — India's tallest dam is Tehri Dam (260.5 m) on the Bhagirathi in Uttarakhand. Option B is wrong — Hirakud's installed capacity is only ~347 MW; it was built primarily for flood control and irrigation alongside power. Option D is wrong — Asia's largest double-curvature arch dam is Idukki Dam on the Periyar River in Kerala.

questions.stem: The TUNGABHADRA DAM — a major irrigation and hydropower project completed in 1953 near Hospet — was jointly constructed by which two Indian states?

options.option_text: Tamil Nadu and Kerala — Periyar basin sharing arrangement
Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka — across their shared river boundary
Maharashtra and Karnataka — upper Krishna basin coordination
Goa and Karnataka — the river flows through the Western Ghats region

questions.explanation: B is correct. Tungabhadra Dam was a joint venture between the former Hyderabad State (later Andhra Pradesh) and Mysore State (later Karnataka), making it one of India's earliest inter-state cooperative dam projects, built on the Tungabhadra River near Hampi. Option A is wrong — Tamil Nadu and Kerala's shared dispute involves the Mullaperiyar Dam on the Periyar River, not the Tungabhadra. Option C is wrong — Maharashtra's joint projects with Karnataka are on the upper Krishna (e.g., Almatti), not the Tungabhadra. Option D is wrong — Goa shares no major dam project on the Tungabhadra.

questions.stem: Which dam project holds the record for the LARGEST GROSS RESERVOIR STORAGE CAPACITY in India — surpassing even the commonly cited Nagarjuna Sagar Dam?

options.option_text: Indira Sagar Dam on the Narmada River in Narmadapuram, Madhya Pradesh
Nagarjuna Sagar Dam on the Krishna River — straddles AP-Telangana border
Rihand Dam (Govind Ballabh Pant Sagar) on the Son River, Uttar Pradesh
Hirakud Dam on the Mahanadi River — the longest earthen dam in India

questions.explanation: A is correct. Indira Sagar Dam on the Narmada River (MP) has India's largest gross storage capacity at ~12,220 MCM (million cubic metres). Option B is the most tempting distractor — Nagarjuna Sagar (~11,472 MCM) is India's second-largest reservoir, and the similar '-Sagar' suffix causes frequent confusion in exams. Option C is wrong — Rihand Dam (Govind Ballabh Pant Sagar) has ~10,600 MCM, ranking it third. Option D is wrong — Hirakud holds ~8,136 MCM, known more for its extraordinary length than storage capacity.

questions.stem: The BAGLIHAR HYDROELECTRIC PROJECT, whose design Pakistan challenged through World Bank neutral-expert arbitration under the Indus Waters Treaty (2005–2007), is built across which river?

options.option_text: Jhelum River — a western river on which India's project rights are restricted
Ravi River — an eastern river fully allocated to India under the treaty
Chenab River — a western river over which India has only limited rights
Sutlej River — an eastern river on which the Bhakra Dam is built

questions.explanation: C is correct. Baglihar Dam is on the Chenab River in Ramban/Doda district, J&K. Under the Indus Waters Treaty (1960), Chenab is a 'western river' allocated primarily to Pakistan; India may build only run-of-river schemes with restricted storage. The neutral expert ruled mostly in India's favour in 2007. Option A is wrong — the Jhelum hosts India's Uri and Kishanganga HEPs, not Baglihar. Option B is wrong — Ravi is an eastern treaty river allocated to India; Ranjit Sagar (Thein) Dam stands on the Ravi. Option D is wrong — Sutlej is also an eastern river, home to the Bhakra-Nangal complex.

questions.stem: The SUBANSIRI LOWER HYDROELECTRIC PROJECT (2,000 MW) — India's largest hydropower scheme under construction by NHPC — is situated at the inter-state border of which two states?

options.option_text: Sikkim and West Bengal — on the Teesta River in the eastern Himalayas
Manipur and Nagaland — on the Barak River, a major northeastern tributary
Meghalaya and Assam — on the Kopili River, a Brahmaputra left-bank tributary
Arunachal Pradesh and Assam — on the Subansiri River in Northeast India

questions.explanation: D is correct. Subansiri Lower HEP (2,000 MW, NHPC) is on the Subansiri River — a major left-bank tributary of the Brahmaputra — straddling the Arunachal Pradesh–Assam border. Prolonged delays resulted from seismic safety concerns and strong protests by downstream communities in Assam. Option A is wrong — Teesta hydropower projects are in Sikkim and West Bengal. Option B is wrong — the Barak River hosts the proposed Tipaimukh Dam in Manipur, not Subansiri. Option C is wrong — Kopili HEP (NEEPCO) in Assam–Meghalaya is a separate, much smaller project.

questions.stem: The PONG DAM (officially Maharana Pratap Sagar) — one of the highest earthen dams in Asia — is built on which river, and its reservoir carries which international wetland designation?

options.option_text: Beas River in Himachal Pradesh; designated under the Ramsar Convention
Ravi River in Jammu & Kashmir; designated under the Bonn Convention
Chenab River in Himachal Pradesh; listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site
Sutlej River in Punjab; designated under the Barcelona Convention

questions.explanation: A is correct. Pong Dam (Maharana Pratap Sagar) is on the Beas River in Kangra district, Himachal Pradesh. Its reservoir is a designated Ramsar Wetland of International Importance — a critical wintering ground for bar-headed geese, common pochard, and other migratory waterfowl. Option B is wrong — the Ravi hosts Ranjit Sagar (Thein) Dam; the Bonn Convention (CMS) governs migratory species movement, not wetland protection specifically. Option C is wrong — Chenab flows through J&K plains; UNESCO World Heritage covers cultural/natural heritage, not wetlands; and the Chenab is not in HP. Option D is wrong — Sutlej has the Bhakra-Nangal complex; Barcelona Convention covers Mediterranean marine environment.

questions.stem: The KISHANGANGA HYDROELECTRIC PROJECT (330 MW, J&K) diverts water from the Kishanganga River — called Neelum in Pakistan. Pakistan challenged this project at the Permanent Court of Arbitration (2013) because the Kishanganga is a tributary of which western river under the Indus Waters Treaty?

options.option_text: Chenab River — the treaty's largest western river allocated to Pakistan
Ravi River — which India can freely use as an eastern treaty river
Jhelum River — on which Pakistan's Neelum-Jhelum project also operates
Indus River (main stem) — headwater diversion affects Pakistan's farmlands

questions.explanation: C is correct. Kishanganga (Neelum in Pakistan) is a left-bank tributary of the Jhelum River. Pakistan objected because India's inter-basin diversion of the Kishanganga would reduce downstream flow for Pakistan's own Neelum-Jhelum HEP. The Permanent Court of Arbitration (The Hague, 2013) upheld India's right to proceed but mandated a minimum environmental flow condition. Option A is wrong — Chenab is where the Baglihar Dam dispute was settled; Kishanganga does not join the Chenab. Option B is wrong — Ravi is an eastern river fully allocated to India under the treaty, so no PCA-level dispute arises. Option D is wrong — Kishanganga joins the Jhelum before the Jhelum meets the Indus; it is not a direct Indus tributary.
